utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, technicians, interpreters; I believe they can hear me. Yes, I can hear you too. Good morning, counsel for the Prosecution; good morning, counsel for the Defence; good morning, General Krstic. I gather that the appearances are the same, and we will continue in hearing the case, the Prosecutor versus General Krstic. Mr. Cayley will resume his examination. Good morning, Witness. Let me just remind you that you are still under oath. Mr. Cayley, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours; good morning, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Cayley: [Cont'd]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, we finished yesterday on the night of the 12th of July, 1995. You will recall you gave evidence yesterday about discovering a rape of a young woman in progress. I want now to move ahead further on in that evening. I believe you kept on patrolling in and around the areas of the factories; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Judges what else you saw and heard that night, that night of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that night was really awful because the noise up there was very strange. You heard shooting around; you heard people screaming. Another time, you heard shooting and you heard just like cowboys or wolves, people making noises like that. It was very dark, and those refugees who were there were very scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, the shots that you heard, were they local shots or were they shots from far away? Could you tell?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they came from all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're a professional soldier and you're used to hearing shooting. Could you actually detect at all from the sound where any of the firing was happening?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was also in the hills, around our UN compound. But you couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard shooting and then screaming and then the sound of people howling or, I think your exact words were, "just like cowboys or wolves, people making noises like that." At the time, what did you think was happening?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I heard that, I got a real strange feeling that they were hunting people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "hunting people," can you expand on that? Can you explain to the Judges what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean Serb people hunting Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they were hunting them, when they found them, what did you think they were doing to them at the time? What were your thoughts at the time?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after that you heard shots, so they were probably basically killing those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I think you patrolled all that night. Do you recall what you were wearing --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that night?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing my full armour; I had my weapon with me, my helmet, my body armour, my ammunition, the standard issue for a soldier. That's what I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you wearing anything that was coloured blue?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was my helmet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your helmet was coloured blue?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that equipment remain with you all night?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened? Can you tell what happened to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later that night, there were some Serb soldiers and they took some equipment from my other fellow soldiers. Later on, they approached me and they asked me to give up my weapon, my body armour, my helmet, and I said no. Later on, they asked again and I said, again, no. Then there was a Serb soldier who took his AK-47, he loaded his weapon, pointed it at my head and asked me again to give up all my stuff, all my equipment, otherwise I would be shot. So I gave him my equipment, my weapon, my body armour, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that happen to anybody else that night?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost everybody who was staying out that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, if you can, how many Dutch soldiers that happened to?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about 30 people, 30 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 30 soldiers had all of their equipment stolen --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- by the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next day, to the 13th of July of 1995. What did you do that day, first thing in the morning; can you recall?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing that I did was I went back to the base to get some food, and then I went back to the human barricade. Because I was unarmed, I tried to get a weapon on the base. They gave me a sidearm, a pistol. And when I went out of the base, I thought to myself that I had better leave it on the base, because if I went out, they would probably steal it again. So I left it right in front of the gate with a colleague of mine. So I went without weapons or anything outside again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you stated you went back to the human barricade. Can you describe to the Judges what you saw taking place from your location there that day?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later that day, early in the morning, the Serb soldiers were preparing to start the transportation again. The buses and the trucks came, and the whole thing started all over again, the same as the day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "to start the transportation again," can you explain to the Judges what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean by that taking the women and children away, separating the men from the women again and children. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you compared the speed of the process that was happening on the 13th of July, compared to the 12th of July, which was faster? Was it faster on the 12th or on the 13th, or was it the same speed?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the 13th, it was faster. They rushed through the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you see any VRS, members of the Bosnian Serb army, that you recognised that day?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I showed yesterday a picture of a man who was sitting next to General Mladic, that man was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, if the witness could just be shown tab 11, which is Exhibit 28/13, 13.1, so that we can just be sure of that individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll carry on so as not to waste any time. You were standing at a location, the human barricade, you said yesterday, very close to the White House. Did you look over to the White House at all that day?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what you saw?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they also rushed out the men, so all the men had to stay at the White House. Some of them went also back inside the White House, Muslim soldiers -- Muslim men with Serb soldiers. Some of them came out also beaten up, scars on their face, bruises on their face, on their arms. But it was as extreme as the day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anything significant that you saw that day by the White House? Did you hear anything by the White House that was significant that day?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They took somebody outside, took him around behind the White House, two Serb soldiers who took a Muslim man outside the building, the White House, took him behind the White House. Then I heard one single shot, and only those two Serb soldiers came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just look at the photograph that's on the ELMO next to you. If the witness could be shown that photograph very quickly. You mentioned a moment ago that that morning, the 13th of July, you saw a VRS officer, and I think you identified this gentleman yesterday. Is this the same individual that you saw on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the man [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's Exhibit 13.1, and it's the individual on the right-hand side of General Mladic. Now, in terms of transportation of individuals, and you said you saw the transportation continuing on the 13th, was it only women and children that were transported on that day, or men, women, and children? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they took some buses from the normal transportation. They took one or sometimes two buses. They drove to the White House, they put the men inside, and they drove away. And about 15, 20 minutes later, they came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they came back, were the buses still full or were they empty?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall what direction the buses drove in?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you saw these buses moving towards Bratunac, and you say that they came back 15 to 20 minutes later. Did you make any conclusion at the time about where those buses had been and stopped and dropped off the men and then returned from?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had the feeling that they were dropped off in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many times that day that process took place? And now I'm talking about the movement of men from Potocari by bus. Do you recall how many busloads?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. I saw it a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "a couple of times," do you mean more than twice, more than three times?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. More than three times, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you can't recall now exactly how many?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time that day the transportation process stopped?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already in the evening, it was about 9.00, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that by that stage, there were no refugees, men, women or children, left in the Potocari area?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see anybody anymore, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the next day, which is the 14th of July, 1995, and I think on that day you were assigned to go to Srebrenica to collect Dutch military equipment from the B Company compound. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges about that journey from Potocari to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had a new assignment that morning, to escort some soldiers from the B Company back to their own compound, to get their military stuff, equipment. So we drove with them, and I saw some horrible things on the way back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Judges what you saw on the road to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- I saw many bodies. It started about 500, 600 metres, when we went out of the gate. To the left and right of the road, we saw dead people. They were already blue and purple because of the heat the day before. Some of them were -- just died from dehydration, and some of them were also shot, you could see that. That was a real awful face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many bodies you saw 500 to 600 metres from the UN compound?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it started with sometimes two, sometimes four, and the further we approached Srebrenica, the number of that went larger and larger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how those bodies were dressed? Were they in military clothing or in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they men only, or were they a mixture of men, women, and children? Do you recall? Do you have any recollection?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of them were older people. Until we approached Srebrenica, we also found men, women, children, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the bodies, as you were on the road to Srebrenica, were mostly older people.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you approached Srebrenica, you say you found men, women, and children who were dead. I now just want to take to you the scene that you saw when you got into the centre of Srebrenica. Can you describe to the Judges what you saw when you got into the centre of town, near to where Bravo Company's compound was located?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we approached the centre of Srebrenica, we call it the blackmarket, the Muslim people had their own blackmarket, it was full of bodies, body parts, lying on each other. They were also blue, purple. Most of them were totally -- I'm sorry. The face of it was not so good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many bodies you saw in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 40, 50 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, how were those bodies dressed, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall the sex of those bodies? Were they a mixture of men and women and children, or were they --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were women and children, some of them were older people, I saw also a few men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you'd collected the equipment from B Company, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back to the UN base in Potocari, and when we came back, they told us that we had to leave also as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you left?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I forgot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after the 14th? Was it a week or two weeks, approximately, or a few days?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So approximately a week after the 14th --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you left Potocari. And where did you go after Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were the last group who went out because we had an agreement that we had -- that we could take our APCs, armoured personnel carriers, with us, and those groups were the last ones to leave the enclave, and that was no problem. And when we approached the iron bridge, we stopped because we couldn't drive any longer with those APCs because they thought that we were doing some action against the Serb army. The only thing we wanted was to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're talking about the iron bridge, you're talking about the bridge over the River Drina into the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, to cut a long story short, I think you eventually made your way back through the Federal Republic, in to Croatia, and then to Zagreb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you flew back to the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Corporal Vaasen, I mean, it's clear from your testimony that you were deeply affected by these terrible things that you saw, and I just would like to ask you if you could share with the Judges how you felt when you immediately got back home to your family and how you now deal with these images five years later.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived at the airport in Holland, at Soesterberg, I was very happy in the first place that I was home, because I saw my family, my girlfriend back. And later on that day, when I was home sitting with my parents, and everybody was gone, my relatives and friends and everybody, you start thinking about what you saw there. And gladly I had some support of my father, because he's also a professional soldier, and I started to cry. Later on, I totally freaked out, started to throw things through the house. Even my own girlfriend couldn't understand what was going on up there. And now, these days, I don't sleep that well. Some days I do, some days I don't. Sometimes I wake up in the middle of the night, totally in a sweat. And every time when I'm alone at home, I always think about what I saw up there. Sometimes I always speak with my colleagues, who also went up there, because the help you get here in Holland, well, they offer it, but it's not something you can put behind your back and forget.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Corporal Vaasen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for the witness. I can now offer him to the Defence for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Now, Corporal Vaasen, you will answer questions that will be -- that the Defence will ask you, but perhaps you would like a break. Are you ready? Do you wish a moment to recuperate, to regain your strength, or would you rather proceed with the cross-examination immediately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At any rate here, take your time, if need be. Mr. Petrusic, I believe it is you who will conduct the cross-examination. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, my learned friends from the Prosecution. Cross-examined by Mr. Petrusic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Corporal Vaasen. Before you arrived in the protected area in January 1995, you underwent special training here in the Netherlands, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you told then what formation of the army of the Republika Srpska was active, was present, in the territory where you were to be posted, that is, in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They told me of all the Serb units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you specifically told which Bosnian Serb army formation was holding that territory?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, we had training here in Holland, they showed those badges, and we also carried a small handpocket, a book, that if we saw Serb units who we couldn't identify, we could look it up in the book, and we always found it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm sorry, but I need to go back to this question specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it said, were you told, which formation of the Bosnian Serb army was holding the territory at that time.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. They didn't tell us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed about the existence of the Muslim units in that territory?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Later on, when we were in the enclave, we were informed that there was an 82nd Muslim Brigade, and there were also other units in the mountains who were under the command of a local commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of the 82nd Brigade, is it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know the name of the local commander of the 82nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I only knew the name of the local commander where I was stationed at, at that location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite sure that it was the 82nd Brigade, or perhaps could it be some other unit?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, because we -- every time when we went on patrol, we also stopped Muslim soldiers who carried weapons. We disarmed them, asked them which unit they were and why we had to take their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in your area of responsibility, were you aware that the area had been demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the meaning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was not demilitarised then.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was demilitarised, but it was very hard for us to find all the weapons of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, that is, your unit, how did you treat armed Muslim formations? What was your attitude to them?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had our standard, normal procedure. We stopped them. When they tried to run away, we went after them. And it's just like in a police arrest; we disarmed them, we searched them. After that, we take every weapon, ammunition, other kind of weapons that they carry, and later on they picked it up from the UN base and went to a barricade in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand. You said that later on they picked it up and went to a barricade in Srebrenica. I don't really understand what you mean. What barricade?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean they had a weapon depot in Srebrenica, the UN soldiers, they had a weapon depot up there, so there were UN soldiers picking those weapons up, what we took away from the Muslim soldiers, and those soldiers, the UN soldiers, took those weapons to the weapon depot in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Corporal Vaasen, during your stay there, or rather when -- during your stay there, how often did it happen, how many times did you have to request that they lay down their weapons?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, please? Once? Twice?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My experience was only two times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were at the observation point "M," OP-M.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Beyond that OP, were there any fortified Muslim positions?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about Captain Enwer yesterday, in yesterday's testimony.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a man from the area, from the village of Jaglici perhaps?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was one of the people who lived in the village Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the formations under his command were in that village, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have their own positions?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They always lived in the village, and sometimes they went up to look at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Captain Enwer was an officer. Could you tell us what was the formation that was under his command?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a local unit. It was not so big; it was about approximately 15 or 20 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, you are a soldier, a professional soldier. Do you think that a unit of 15 to 20 people, to be commanded by a captain -- after all, a captain is a relatively high rank in every army -- so don't you think that to have a captain command such a small unit, which is not larger than a platoon, perhaps, that it is not too much, to have a captain?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how they work in the Muslim army, so I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that on the 10th of July, in the vicinity of your OP, there was an armed clash between the members of the Muslim army themselves?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was later on, when they started to attack the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the attack on the enclave began on the 6th of July, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the 10th of July came later, and I asked you if it was the 10th of July or perhaps some other date.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know why did this clash break out between the Muslim soldiers? Do you know the reason for it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the only experience I had between those groups was only when I was captured in Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any fatalities in that confrontation?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any pressure brought on you and your colleagues by Muslim commanders to take their families towards the base in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no force. We had an agreement with Captain Enwer, and we took those women and children back to the base with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some members of the Muslim army wanted to stay in Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified that there were several hundred Muslim soldiers in Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Jaglici. It was around the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Lehovici.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Several hundred. Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you any numbers. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should like to show this witness his statement of the 11th and 18th of November, 1999, which he gave to the investigators of the International Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will be Exhibit D5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, is this your signature on the first page?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is your statement?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2, in the fifth paragraph on that page, fifth paragraph from the top, the fourth sentence says: "I saw 1.000 to 1.500 Muslim soldiers near the village called Lehovici who were walking in the northerly direction."

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is that the figure, the number of soldiers that you can't remember today?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday, you said that Muslims gathered in Jaglici and that they were short of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew about that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand. You did not know whether they had enough ammunition?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were captured, then they told us about their weapons, their ammunition, and how much they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your platoon was held in captivity for three days, was it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were six members, and we were there for three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why were you captured?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same thing that I said yesterday, because we were UN and, first of all, we were there for their protection, and also as a kind of shield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know -- were you aware of some other cases of the capture of UN members by Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your OP was shelled, or rather when fire was opened on your OP, were there any -- did you suffer any casualties?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your OP damaged in any way, that is, directly hit by a shell?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, our OP was damaged. The first shell of the mortar, it came in the defence wall of our OP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you set off from Jaglici to Potocari, with the local population fleeing, could you tell us how many people were there all in all, that is, women, children, and everybody all told? How many?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we started with a small -- large group -- a small group, and the further we got to Potocari, the bigger the group went. And later, we had some 900 or 1.000 [Realtime transcript read in error "9.000"] people with us, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on your way between Jaglici and Potocari, you were being joined by more people, so that there were 900, 1.000 people.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and maybe more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many men were among them?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not many men. Most of them were old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. In the transcript, it said that there were 9.000 people with you. You didn't say 9.000. [Realtime transcript read in error "JUDGE RODRIGUES:"]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't say 9.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Then it has to be corrected in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 11th, you arrived in Potocari sometime, in some hour of the night, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the night between the 11th and the 12th of July, did you then know anything, have any information about the situation in the base and outside it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I have to interrupt you. It has to be corrected here because Judge Riad was the one who intervened, not Judge Rodrigues. Yes, you may continue, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So we've arrived at the 12th of July now, and I think I was not answered my previous question, I'm afraid, and that is, the night between the 11th and the 12th of the July, my question was whether the witness had any information about that night within and around the compound.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, when you came on duty or when you started your day's work, you saw Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the first time that on the 12th of July you spotted Serb soldiers in that area?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they came later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived about, well, 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that you had spotted Arkan's Tigers there.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. When the Serb army entered the enclave, there were also Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They had a typical insignia.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the following words, "Arkan's Tigers" written on it; am I right?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to Arkan's Tigers, you testified that there were also the Drina Wolves who were there. Can you tell us anything about other soldiers? Judging by their insignia, were they any different from these two formations?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, because the Drina Wolves had a badge with a wolf and there were also regular soldiers, and they had regular badges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "regular badges"?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we searched in our pocketbook, and it was a normal sign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Arkan's Tigers -- excuse me, the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm sorry to interrupt you. I'm not referring to Arkan's Tigers or the Drina Wolves here. I'm interested in other soldiers belonging to other units. Could you be more precise as to the badge they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was some kind of crown, and there were also the letters "HVO" on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the soldiers that came in with dogs? Did you notice their badges?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any police units, uniformed police units there?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated in evidence that the two formations we mentioned went from house to house, looting them, taking property away, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I recall that's not what the witness said yesterday, and I think it should be clear both for the purposes of the record and the witness. The witness actually said yesterday, and I have it written in my notes, I recall from my notes, that it was the Drina Wolves who were actually clearing houses above the road. I think the witness can clarify that for the Court, but I do not believe he said that Arkan's Tigers were clearing houses above the road. But I think the witness can probably answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, how do you respond to this objection by Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, Your Honour. Let me check it in my notes. I should need probably more time for checking the record. But I believe that Mr. Cayley is right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, we can solve this dilemma with a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it only the Drina Wolves who looted the houses, or were there any other units in the area as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic, you can ask that question of the witness. He was referring to Drina Wolves. You can also ask him whether there was any other formations as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, were there any other units looting those houses?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, those units, that is, the soldiers from those units, threw incendiary bullets and grenades in those houses.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a professional soldier and I'm a layperson in that respect, but I do have some knowledge about it. As far as I know, when you throw an incendiary grenade, the whole area catches fire. In this case, it would be the whole house.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated yesterday, while you were shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 5/19, I should like to show you the same exhibit again, the same document, 5/19, and 5/5. Mr. Vaasen, are these the houses that were broken into by Serb soldiers at the time?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can conclude that there is not a single burnt house here, in this particular area.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but I don't know how old the picture is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This picture is a Prosecutor's Exhibit, and as far as I can tell, it was taken on the 7th of June, 1996.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put Exhibit 5/5 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a broader picture of the area on this exhibit, but the locality is the same. We can once again conclude that there are no burnt houses on this photograph. Is that correct, Mr. Vaasen? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, but I don't know how old this picture is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence doesn't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can perhaps clarify a few matters. We're going to find out the exact dates. I do know that 5/5 is a helicopter shot that was taken long, long, long after these events. Mr. Petrusic, I'm sure, will also recall that when Mr. Ruez was testifying, he stated that in a number of these photographs that were taken where there is a date in the bottom right-hand corner, that they couldn't operate the date switches on the camera, and so that date may also be wrong. And although this witness cannot testify, Mr. Petrusic, I'm sure, is also well aware that many buildings were rebuilt in all areas of Bosnia long after the events with which we're discussing have taken place. So for the purposes of the record, these are not contemporary photographs that were taken immediately -- at the time of the event or immediately thereafter, and I will find out from my colleagues the exact date when these photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you, Mr. Cayley. We are not going to open a debate here. We're just hearing the evidence at this moment. The witness is merely answering questions. But be that as it may, the Chamber is grateful for this clarification from you, Mr. Cayley. There will be questions by the Judges as well with the purpose of elucidating the matter, this one and others. Thank you very much, Mr. Cayley. Mr. Petrusic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vaasen, speaking of the houses, the ones that we have just seen on the ELMO, I should like to know whether you saw any civilians on that day, that is, before the incursion of Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you had seen Serb soldiers looting the houses, and you also said that they were shooting and that you saw them taking drugs, if I'm correct in understanding your evidence.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain that to us a little bit? Maybe the information I have is somewhat different. Could you explain this particular situation to us? They were breaking into these houses, they were shooting, they were taking drugs, everything at the same time, or ...

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the same time. It was very clearly that the men who went inside, they came out with typewriters, telephones, and other stuff, I said that already yesterday, and they also -- I saw them take a lot of alcohol, we call it slivovitz. They also offered that to some of us; we refused it. Sometimes they took a break and started to drink and sniff cocaine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were there, in their immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Our orders were to observe them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any orders to prevent them from engaging in these types of activities?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any order like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that there had been several wounded persons to whom you offered assistance when Serb soldiers started shooting on the refugees, first of all, above their heads and then on them, and you told us that they sustained injuries on their limbs.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two female persons; one of them was shot in the leg and the other one was also shot in the leg and in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the UN base, there were some wounded people.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps suggest or do something about the transport of these wounded persons to the base?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think this is a convenient moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic, for this suggestion. We are now going to have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, before the evacuation of refugees from Potocari began, could you tell us how many people were there, in your estimate?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned to the UN compound, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You return to the base on the 11th of July. So the evacuation started on the 12th of July, sometime in the afternoon. And at that time, before the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many people, thousands of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many men were there? I mean, between the ages of 18 onward.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many men were separated and taken to the White House, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th and the 13th of July, General Mladic visited that area, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrived at -- actually, I saw him on the 12th of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him on the 13th as well?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the officer that was shown on that photograph yesterday and the day before yesterday, that was Exhibit 28/13, so the officer sitting to the left of General Mladic, we see it on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you also see him on the 12th and the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether your impression was that, in the absence of General Mladic, it was this man, this officer, who played the main role, who had the main say in that area?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm about to finish, but before I do so, I should like to go back to the incident of the 12th of July, in the evening, that is, the rape, as described by the witness, the rape which took place behind the factory compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, you're also a medical worker, you're a paramedic, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was dark, but when you switched on the lamp, then you saw bruises on her thighs.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, do you -- would you think that, from a medical point of view, some time must elapse between receiving a blow until the emergence of a bruise?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if one concludes that that girl was beaten, that she suffered a blow on her thighs, don't you think that there is a certain time lag between the blow and the bruise?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you hit somebody or forced somebody to do things, then actually it started real fast, the blue things on her legs, the bruises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Corporal Vaasen, how many hanged men did you see?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were two persons; one was lying on the girl and the other was standing guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was about men who had hanged themselves.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the factory, yes, I saw a couple of men, yes, who had hanged themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw three or four men hanging there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the evacuation began, the men were being separated on the basis of some criterion. Was it age?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they started about the age of 16, 17 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the others boarded the buses.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The men who got separated got boarded on the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many convoys were escorted by members of UN forces?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to conclude, Corporal Vaasen, on the 14th of July, when you went to Srebrenica, who were you with on that occasion? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were mixed up with B Company, and I don't know those soldiers by name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Corporal Vaasen. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Judge Riad. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. President. [In English] Corporal Vaasen, good morning.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I have a few questions to clarify some points, although you have been quite clear. You mentioned that on the 12th of July, you saw the Serb army, I'm almost quoting you, coming from Bratunac, heavily armed with RPGs, with anti-tank weapons, with Russian-type tanks. Is this a Serb army or a Bosnian Serb army? What kind of army was it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had the marks -- the badges from the HVO, and the soldiers who were walking in front of them were Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Arkan's Tigers.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And was it -- you said it was quite a substantial power, a substantial force. Was there a situation -- did the situation require such a force? Was there a real battle there? Were the Bosnian forces equivalent to have all this military force?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was not.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now that you mentioned the Arkan's Tigers, you seem to be quite acquainted with the insignias, you can know the insignia of the Arkan Tigers, you know the insignia of the Drina Wolves, as we saw --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: -- and then you mentioned something called regular soldiers.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Does it mean that the Drina Wolves were not regular soldiers? Were they an independent unity under independent command?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mean they were not subject to the same higher command?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They could have their own policy.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in these events, several events which you mentioned, for instance, certain events which -- like the burning of the houses, the plundering of the houses, throwing phosphorous grenades, and the other one where you were stopped and they told you that if they kill one or two more, it doesn't make any difference, when you interfered and told them to stop what they were doing, was it the Drina Corps which was visible?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And were you close enough to know?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Because in the case of the people who you said stopped you and laughed at you and threatened you not to interfere, you were close enough in that case. But in the case of the plundering of the houses and the phosphorus and so on, were you close enough to know that they were the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You were not.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Then how did you detect that it was the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the same group that went inside was also the same group we stopped -- tried to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And the group you tried to stop was Drina.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, these Drina Wolves, these Drina Wolves, as you said, they were an independent unit. Was it disciplined, as disciplined as the army? Was it organised under very strict command, or just a band of anarchic fighters?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from my point of view, they looked like bandits. They were just doing something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean, everything can do what he likes, or were they receiving orders?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen that they received orders. I saw only that they went to those houses and started plundering, shooting, throw grenades, and they enjoyed themselves real good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So it did not give you the impression of a disciplined -- you are an army man -- of a disciplined unit of the army.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not so quite disciplined as the rest of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The Arkan Tigers were different?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The Arkan Tigers were supposed to be Bosnian Serbs or more or less Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can recall, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Serbs. You mentioned also something about hunting Muslim people and killing them when they were found. These hunts, were also the Drina Corps involved in it?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it. I only heard the screams and the noises, the shots, the sound of a wolf, but I presumed it was the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: In all these events, have you had a glimpse of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You also mentioned that in the centre -- I think, yes, it was yesterday -- in the centre of Srebrenica, or perhaps today, the blackmarket, what you called the blackmarket, was full of bodies, 40 to 50 people, and they were civilians, women, children, and old people.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Have you found out what caused this great mass murder?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew that Bravo Company, who was stationed in Srebrenica, had to withdraw back to the blackmarket, to the square, and they had to stand there and to help Muslim people, because they were scattered around there. And I also -- I was also informed that most of the people were killed during the retreat to the UN base in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean, this was in the blackmarket.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean, women and children, what is the relation between this and the retreat of the army?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Bravo Company had also suffered from heavy fire, and when they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Fire directed towards the civilians.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians, and also on UN soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: From where? Who?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the hills.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: From the hills. And who was in the hills?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But not the Drina Corps, you cannot --

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: -- determine.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you said every time you met Muslim units, you disarmed them and took their weapons. Was there any clash between your forces, between the UN, and the Muslim fighters, or was it -- or did they comply with your orders?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they weren't happy with those orders, but we were very clear that they had to give up those weapons. It's the agreement that we made with them, so they couldn't do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But you were not ordered to do the same thing with the others, with the other Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Corporal Vaasen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Riad. Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Corporal, when you first came to the Srebrenica area and you were at OP Mike, were you aware of which part of the Bosnian Serb army was in authority in that area? I mean, did somebody tell you that it was this battalion or this corps, so that you knew who you were dealing with?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: They didn't tell you -- nobody said that "This is such and such a battalion" or "such and such a corps of the Bosnian Serb army that's in control"?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But you did mention several other times in your testimony that you knew somebody was the Drina Corps, you mentioned in answering Judge Riad's questions. So at what point did you become aware that there were soldiers from the Drina Corps in the area?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was very clear the day that they arrived. They had the badges on their shoulders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You're talking the day you arrived where, in Potocari or in the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing at the human barricade when they arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. So before that, you had no idea, for instance, that the soldiers who were shelling the OP posts, et cetera, you didn't know to what battalion or corps they belonged?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You mentioned that the people in the Potocari compound got even more scared, I think you said, when they found out that both the Arkan Tigers and the Drina Wolves were there. What was there about the Drina Wolves that would be likely to make the refugees feel even more scared than other soldiers being there?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we -- the expression of their faces was very clear, that when they arrived, they got more scared and more nervous, and the tension -- the feeling of them, you could feel it even also there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: In your knowledge, to your knowledge, had you heard things that would make you, if you had been a refugee, to feel more apprehensive about the Drina Wolves? Did they have a special reputation of some sort?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And were you aware when you saw the Drina Wolves that the Drina Wolves were somehow part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You were aware of that. My second question is when you went back to Srebrenica, you told us you went back there, and when you saw the terrible sight of all the bodies, who, to your knowledge or in your observation, was left living in Srebrenica? I mean, were there any Muslim civilians left that you know about? Were there some Serbs left? Who was left in the village of Srebrenica after the evacuations from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after the evacuation of Potocari, it was real fast, because when those Muslim refugees were gone, the Serb people were standing -- yes, were standing right in front of the gate to enter the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That was Potocari, right?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: How about Srebrenica? When you went back to Srebrenica and saw all the dead bodies, were there any living people around there still living in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: It was an empty town, so far as you could tell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. The same thing you started to answer in Potocari. Once all the evacuations were finished on the 14th, you were left in Potocari for another week. To the best of your observation, who else was left in Potocari, either in the compound or in the houses or areas around the compound?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure that only the Dutch Battalion, the UN Battalion, was there, and I also saw that Serb people, civilians, were also going into the enclave, plundering, and I saw them even go back -- they went in with cars -- with empty cars, and they came back with washing machines, VCRs, everything that they found on the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: During that week that you were left in the compound in Potocari, did you see any Muslim civilians of any sort, men, women, children, old, young, anybody?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Corporal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. Corporal Vaasen, I also have a few questions for you. You spoke about Arkan's Tigers, Drina Wolves, dog handlers, and regular troops. When you mentioned those regular troops, in answering one of Mr. Petrusic's questions, you said that they had a particular badge with a crown on it, and you also stated that the letters "HVO" were on it. Are you absolutely certain about that, that those were, indeed, the letters "HVO" or rather could it have been some other letters?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, you could clearly see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "HVO".

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not want to lead you in any manner, but let me just tell you that the letters "HVO" are used in the context of Croatian soldiers. Here, we are dealing with Bosnian Serb soldiers. Having said that, I should like to know whether you are still sure that the letters in question were, indeed, "HVO".

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because they had different kinds of clothes. They also had our clothes already. They had their regular uniforms and they also were dressed in those uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Usher, could you check whether Exhibit 5/19 is still on the ELMO, please. As regards this particular photograph, Corporal Vaasen, I should like to ask you the following question: You see a number of houses here on the photograph. Could you tell us whether the state of repair of these houses is the same as the one that you saw at the time, when houses were being torched, or do you think that there is any difference between the situation now and then?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you anyway. I think that you have already said this in response to my colleague's question, but let me ask it once again. Do you know General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have never seen General Krstic in the field, or anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And my last question for you. You are a military man and you are accustomed to functioning within an organisation, and you respect discipline. If we take these two elements into account, organisation and discipline, and bearing in mind your experience and what you were able to observe in the area at the relevant time, in your opinion, was there any organisation in the events you told us about? Was there any discipline as well?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the deportation of the Muslim refugees, there was some kind of discipline. But for the rest of it, there was no discipline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about the level of organisation? Did you have an impression that there, indeed, had been an organisation which was behind this discipline?

utterances.speaker: DAVID VAASEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much, Corporal Vaasen, for coming here to testify before the International Tribunal. We know you have just had to experience once again your ordeal. Let me say once again that the Chamber is thankful for your testimony, and I hope that you will be able, one day, to find peace in this beautiful country of yours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before we let the witness go, I should like to know the status of Exhibit 57 and Defence Exhibit D5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Exhibit 57 is the patch which the witness identified as having seen on the arm of a member of the Drina Wolves. If there are no objections from the Defence, I'd like to apply for that -- for admission into evidence of that exhibit, please. And we certainly have no objections in respect of Exhibit D5, which is the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Cayley. Mr. Petrusic, are there any objections as regards the admission of Exhibit 57? And do you wish to tender D5 into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we do not object to the exhibit tendered by Mr. Cayley. However, I should -- could you please repeat your second question, Your Honour, as regards this other exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I thought you were going to ask for your exhibit, D5, to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Exhibits 57 and D5 will be admitted into evidence, Mr. Dubuisson. Very well, then. Corporal Vaasen, you have heard a number of questions by the Prosecutor, by the Defence, and by the Judges as well. At the end of your testimony, I should like to know whether there is anything else that you wish to add to what you have said here in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Corporal Vaasen, once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon or Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We do have another witness, Mr. President, but you might feel it's the appropriate time to take a break because we have to rearrange ourselves here. And rather than do that in front of the Judges, it may be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dubuisson has drawn my attention to a particular fact. For the purposes of the public principle of the hearing, I should like to know whether your next witness is a protected one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: He is a protected witness, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry to insist, but I should like to know what the reasons for his application are and what kind of protective measures you're seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Actually, I think my colleague Mr. McCloskey will answer the question, but it might be an idea that we go into closed session before he actually discusses the reason for the protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the public gallery, I should therefore stress that our next witness will be testifying in closed session, and we will now go into private session to discuss the reasons for his seeking protective measures. Are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We're ready for the next witness, who I believe will be Witness F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has it been resolved yet? Could you repeat, please, from the beginning, Mr. McCloskey, because I was not getting the French interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe this is Witness F that we are ready for, and we are all ready to go.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, this will be Witness F, and there is nobody in the public gallery of this hearing. The debate can be followed on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, he will be testifying in Dutch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a preliminary question. Mr. McCloskey, will you be showing any exhibits on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could move -- then perhaps the interpreter and the witness could change places, so that the witness is closer to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's an excellent idea. Could we try that out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please put your headsets on? Could you please switch places? Will you put your earphones on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He needs a headset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me, Witness F? You can hear? Very well. Witness F, that is what we shall call you, in view of the protective measures that have been granted to you. You will now read the solemn declaration which the usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now the interpretation for the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will perform my duty professionally and with full respect for confidentiality.
