utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness F, thank you for coming. The registrar will now show you a piece of paper with your name on it. You will only say if this is your name or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is your name. Very well. Now you will answer questions which the Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey, will be asking of you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, you are currently a member of the Dutch army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1995, were you assigned as a peacekeeping mission in Bosnia as a Dutch soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone or speak up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can the witness please get a little closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I left in January for Potocari, in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your mission in Bosnia at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Our mission was humanitarian, the disarming of any Muslim fighters we might find, reconnaissance duties, patrols along the border area and between the OPs in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What OPs were you assigned to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: My main OPs were mainly OP Papa, at the main entrance to the enclave, and later on OP ^ Sierra.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever work with Corporal Vaasen on an OP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: No, I have never been with Vaasen on an OP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. McCloskey, the interpreters say that they did not understand the question. So could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should -- and I should now like to seize the opportunity to say that we have yet one more mediator in our chain of interpretation and communication. So will you please pause between every question and answer because we have to take a number of relays. We now have a second relay here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, normally, we need to make a pause between the question and answer, but in this case, according to what Mr. Dubuisson tells us, we also have to make at least two pauses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work with Corporal Vaasen on any of the OPs during your time in the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: No, I have never been with Corporal Vaasen. I've never worked with him on an OP. I've never worked with Corporal Vaasen on an OP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the kinds of military weapons you saw that the Muslim army had at the various times that you were working there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The Muslim army consisted of mainly lightly armed military, mortars, hand mortars, AK-47s of Russian make, hand grenades, shell hand grenades, and light machine-guns, and some pistols. They also had self-made weapons, home-made weapons. They were very creative, and most of those weapons were in the compound in Srebrenica, on stock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice a change in the quantity or quality of their weaponry as we get closer to July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The more the situation of tension came near by and the pressure in the area arose, we suspected that there were helicopter droppings, and after that we saw men in better military uniforms, they had better arms, better weapons, they had new shoes, they had better equipment, and certainly they were better prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any large equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Not so much. Most of the large material had been confiscated by the 12th Battalion at the time, and it was in the compound in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any armour in the hands of the Muslim soldiers prior or during the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: One time, when I arrived at the beginning of January, I saw one Muslim fighter with an AK, and he ran off as fast as he could. That was the only thing I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the Muslim army with a tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: One time, one of my colleagues observed a tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see it personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Negative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On July 11th, when the town of Potocari fell, what was your assignment that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: On that day, we were understaffed already. We had worked hard, we were together, and we had to take extra duties on the OP and in the compound. And my place was a certain place in the building with a machine-gun post, directed towards OP Papa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That place was not in the large corridor, but in a separate building, with a view to the northern side of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how high up were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: On the second floor of the building. The building only consisted of two floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time, I would like to show the witness the Exhibit 5/2. If you can put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could look directly at the exhibit as opposed to the ELMO, you may get a better look at it. And if you could study it for a moment. Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the area outlined in yellow the UN base, as it's marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see the area of the UN base where you were actually located on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take the green marking pencil that's in front of you and circle the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you put your initials next to that? Actually, strike that. Just put "F" next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, about what time did you first go to that lookout spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Early in the morning, after we had gotten the orders, the weapons were distributed and the equipment, and the task duties were given out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point in the day, did you notice activity, military activity, in the area where you were watching out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct. There was more and more shooting in the area. We heard heavy engine sounds from all directions, especially from the northern direction. At the eastern side, there was heavy battery sound, but on that day, they mostly came from the northern side, ever more engine sounds, smoke, shooting. From time to time, we saw Muslim fighters with mortars. They just fired them and then they ran back. And that's how it went for quite a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the area on this exhibit where you could see Muslim fighters with mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I can't see the Muslim fighters, but I know the area, of course. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just point out the area where you saw the Muslim fighters with mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Indicates]. Here and here and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The record should indicate that he indicated he saw Muslim fighters on both sides of the UN base, up in the hill area, as well as the northern side of the UN base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you describe the scene as you witnessed it that morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That morning, I was with my colleague, we went to fetch water, and we saw more and more movements of those Muslim fighters. They were grouping themselves and redisappeared into the woods. From our point, viewing point, we saw, towards the direction of houses and OP Papa, we heard fighting coming from there, fighting sounds. And later that day, and I don't know the exact times, more Serbs started coming in. We saw smoke arise around OP Papa and on both sides of the hill, more shooting, more heavy engine sounds, tank sounds. And the Muslim fighters were very nervous, and they started to disappear into the woods, they ran off. On the eastern side, there were a couple of Muslim fighters firing mortars at, I think, Serb materiel, and they were taken under heavy machine-gun fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to photograph the smoke in the area of OP Papa that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes. My position was such that I had a good view at the incoming materiel, the infantry, in such a way that I also saw the houses at OP Papa's main entrance. And indeed, I had a couple of pictures in my camera, I took pictures of houses on fire and the smoke of a tank, a Russian tank's oil fire -- I'm sorry, oil smoke, very heavy smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we present the witness with Exhibit 63.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this -- does this photograph depict what you were able to photograph that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you point at the various smoke plumes that you see and tell us anything that you can about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: This was my position [indicates]. This was a hill with mainly Serb positions. They also had cannons which had been observed before --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. When you point to something, we have to get it on the record, so please listen carefully to the question and try to answer the question as particularly as you can. Could you first point to the smoke that you noticed and tell us what you can about the various smoke plumes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: These are smoke plumes arising from houses. In this area -- there was OP Papa in this area. In this area [indicates] we had an open field which was behind OP Papa. Here on this hill, against this hill, were Serb positions. We were told that there was a minefield here [indicates], and later on it turned out not to be true. This smoke plume came from a T-55 tank, a Russian tank --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, again. Can the record reflect that there is a dark smoke plume in the middle of the photograph that the witness has described as coming from a tank. And that the mountain behind the smoke he earlier described is an area where there were Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other smoke in the area, can you describe what you believe that to be from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Those other smoke plumes came from houses in that area. Most of them were set afire. It shows clearly from the white smoke plumes, it was very dry in that area, so those houses burnt with white smoke and not with dark smoke. Dark smoke comes from oil. And behind this tree line here [indicates], all those fires were set ablaze. Sometimes we even saw the flames. And those are the only pictures I took from this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, the witness was pointing to the more whitish smoke plume on the right side of the picture, and then going even more over to the right, describing the smoke he was able to see and sometimes flames.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw shortly after taking this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Well, what we observed was very nervous Muslim fighters at the time, sounds -- the tank and materiel sound coming closer. Along the tree line, along the fields, there came a very well-organised group of infantry units with a tank before them. This tank which I showed you, the tank with the dark smoke, it was indeed a Russian tank of the type T-55. And to the left of the compound, there were organised military men, and to the right, also organised military, and they cleansed all the houses and looted everything that they could take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this first wave of what you've described as organised soldiers, what they were wearing, what they looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: This first wave of an organised army consisted of well-disciplined infantry. They were dressed with helmets, beautiful, good camouflage suits, well-armed. They had several commanders, at least NCOs, who gave orders. They had good liaison materiel. The units were posted on both sides of the enclave and they had contact. That is how they advanced in line. And it was -- I had the impression that they were very well-organised, and I think I have enough experience to judge this after my time in service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour were their camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: On the right side of the compound from -- to my right-hand side, most of them were dressed in black. They were big, strong boys, strong guys, lightly armed. They had very good liaison materiel, carried on their backs mainly, and most of them were dressed in black. They also cleansed all the houses very thoroughly. And to the left, there was mainly infantry. They advanced across the field. To the left, there were fewer houses than to the right, so there were infantry in camouflage suits, helmets. They had machine-guns, AK-47s, grenades. It was an infantry unit, an ordinary infantry unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. You just mentioned also that they cleansed all the houses very thoroughly. I want to know the meaning of this word. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They cleansed or cleared the houses in such a way that they could be certain that there were no Muslim fighters or other people left behind. Their task was cleaning or cleansing out the whole area so that the units coming after them could advance through this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what colour camouflage did the unit you'd last described wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was this first wave of soldiers all dressed in black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: To my right-hand side, yes, and they cleared out all the houses. And to the other side, there was infantry in camouflage and armed. To the right-hand side, there was more fighting than to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the soldiers on the left, they were also dressed in black; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the others dressed as?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Camouflage suits with helmets, and they were under the direct command of a group commander, sergeant, or a corporal, about that rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers in green camouflage together with the soldiers in black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Not at first, until they had advanced halfway towards the compound. If I could show it in a picture, but I don't have a picture here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, we've gone back to Exhibit 5/2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: So at first, those men dressed in black came along this line [indicates], they advanced along this line, and they had several fighting incidents with the Muslim fighters --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry to interrupt, but for the record I have to show you that you're talking about from the bottom of the photo up towards the UN base, that is where the black soldiers advanced.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: So here were the soldiers dressed in black, and here was the organised army advancing in this direction as a corporal or a sergeant. Those black military men also advanced, and they cleared or cleansed out all the houses, and they organised themselves, or regrouped, around this spot [indicates] --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indicating right where the "UN base" words are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: So they organised here [indicates], military men in camouflage suits also advanced from this direction, from this hill down [indicates], so this whole area --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, for the record, we have to say from the hill on the left side of the photograph, military people in camouflage are advancing down towards the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but could you please ask the witness where was the position and the direction from which the photograph was taken, that is, Exhibit 63, if you could do that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you tell the Court where your photograph was taken from and what direction the photograph -- what direction you were pointing the camera in when you took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Towards this direction [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. First can you tell us where you were when you took the photograph. Is that inside the little circle marked "F"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct, in this dark building, which you see here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you take your pointer again and point in the direction -- or just lay the pointer down in the direction your photograph was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the record should indicate he's pointing straight down to the bottom of the photograph. And that's in the direction of Bratunac, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you saw these soldiers going into these houses, did you see them taking any property or doing anything that you thought was not soldierly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: This first wave mostly cleared out the houses, and they were certainly trained to do so. Immediately afterwards, there were some people who entered the houses and who took all their belongings, everything that was valuable, they just carried outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe who those people were, how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: They were dressed in camouflage. They were less well-organised. They were not under any direct command. They had -- so after this first infantry line had been through, they had to guard this area because there might still be some resistance, and they literally just spoiled themselves with other people's property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were both these units you've described Bosnian Serb army units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to watch all of this from your perch on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct. It was an ideal point, looking towards the north and the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see other soldiers, other Bosnian Serb soldiers, arrive in the area while you were still up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes. The units were replenished, more materiel was coming in, kind of replenishing units came in to replenish the troops advancing towards Srebrenica, bringing in more materiel. There were also officers amongst them and higher ranks, because this area was already cleared because the others had been through. And those units mainly consisted of what I would call Rambo-types, not disciplined units, and perhaps some reserve people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: They were mainly dressed in camouflage and also civilian, so most of them had camouflage trousers and a civilian shirt. It was a hot day. And this type of military were less well-trained physically. They were a bit fatter, they had bellies. They were also older than the first wave. They also had AK-47s with wooden butts, pistols. They had bandannas. The men with the machine-guns carried the machine-gun straps diagonally across their chest. They were smoking, they had cigarettes between their lips. So they were less disciplined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see other types of units come into the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: When the first wave had passed the compound and the Rambo-types were around, were supposed to keep the area safe, more vehicles came in, military and civilian vehicles, also police vehicles, "police" was written on those vehicles. And I saw a blue tank which was very distinctive between all those blue -- between all those green. There were military polices, also some reporters, people in civilian clothes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this blue vehicle that you saw, was it a tank or an armoured personnel carrier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: It was not a tank. It was a vehicle on normal wheels, ordinary wheels. It's an armed vehicle to transport personnel. About 15 men would be transported with such a vehicle. Usually it's slightly armed with a machine-gun, such a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other blue vehicles in the vicinity of Potocari that day of a military type?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Negative. Only the police cars. Most of them were Gulfs, Volkswagen Gulfs, type 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers in a blue military-style outfit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct. They were dressed in blue uniforms, or jumpsuits, overalls with a black belt and pistol, and an AK. And some of them had an automatic weapon of German origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first see these men in blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Later that day, after the first wave had passed and the compound was surrounded, and most people were there before, in front of the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these Bosnian Serb soldiers, these people in blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: They were certainly Serbian police, army police, yes. They were subordinate to the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see how these Serb army police acted throughout the day? Could you tell what role they played in the events of this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: They were present, mainly. Some of them entered the compound in order to look at the refugees, and my idea was that their task was mainly to secure the higher ranking officers, to keep them safe. I think a kind of military police, a kind of anti-terrorist unit, who had to guard the higher ranking people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it true that you remember these days as the first day, meaning the day that the Bosnian Serb soldiers arrive, and the second day, meaning the day that all the refugees were shipped out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I may have misstated the date, Mr. President, on this, but we will just refer to this as the first day, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay up in your post on that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: A couple of hours. And the day before that first day, we were also already there. We were understaffed, so I think -- I don't know the time anymore, but perhaps till about noon, around that time, we stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On that first day that the soldiers arrived, what did you do after leaving the lookout area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: After the Serbs had entered and the compound had been surrounded, we got orders to lay down our arms and to make ourselves visible, to show ourselves to the Serb units, to show that we would not use any violence against them, as a sign of that. We had to go out into the open and just wait and see what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the order to lay down your arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The order came from, at that time, my commander, Major Otter, and he, of course, also gets his orders from a higher hand, and it just filtered down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, were you able to assist the refugees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes. We were already understaffed, and there had been so many refugees that we had to give them help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how you personally helped them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The refugees had, of course, already arrived on our compound, and during the night, we tended to them, we comforted them. And the day when the arms were laid down, everybody went their own way. There was no direct chain of command anymore, and actually everybody assisted as they could. I myself mainly -- well, it's probably not a proper expression, but what I did was put people on the buses, on trucks, on tractors. I was in command at the time, I was in the rank of a commander, so I -- there was no direct chain of command in this whole process, in this whole situation. So I directed others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you help any refugees with their children or problems they had with their children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Correct. More and more refugees came into the compound. If I could just show you on the map from which direction. Our people had made a hole in the gate, in the fence, and the refugees came from this direction [indicates], onto the compound, and I was positioned in this area at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. May the record show that you're speaking to an area just below the "Y" in "Blue Factory" on the outline of the yellow border of the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Many women and children came, many babies, mostly babies, with babies, babies who had swollen up. It was save yourselves. Older people were left behind. Everybody was just trying to get to safety, onto the compound. And several times, I held babies in my arms which were so swollen that they finally died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us any kind of an estimate of how many deceased babies you had to take like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: About between 5 and 15, and perhaps even more. I didn't count at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the babies alive that were given you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes, some of them were still alive, but they were certainly undernourished. Usually the women would give me the babies because they just didn't know anymore what to do and what their future would bring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to care for some of the babies that were still alive and get them some care?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I, in turn, gave those babies to our medical staff, who at that point in time cared for the wounded, for the refugees, and for babies and children. I mainly was concerned with helping people into the compound, and I gave the babies to the medical staff and I referred them to the medical staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after that period where you were helping refugees into the compound, did you eventually go over to the area where people were being loaded on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: There was chaos on the compound. There were several buses, trucks, tractors. There was nobody in charge. It was a very hot day. There was no water, no food. We ourselves had flasks with water, and I ordered some of my colleagues and subordinates to get water and to distribute it to the refugees. The Serb soldiers just stood there, looking, and they just liked what they saw. Some of them were robbing us, the DutchBat soldiers, of our pistols, of our helmets. They took away our watches, our clothing, just for a souvenir. Those were mainly those Rambo-types which I described coming in the second wave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when Muslims were actually loaded onto buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw of that process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The people who were loaded into the buses and onto the trucks were mainly the people outside the compound. They wanted to get them away as fast as possible. A separation was made between men between the ages of 14, 15, up to 50. The men had to surrender their belongings. And the women were transported in the other direction, towards the buses. They had to advance towards the first bus, and that is how they filled all the buses. And as soon as a bus was full, two or three buses left the enclave. Sometimes they were escorted by a military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the men were separated, did you see where they went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Some buses, a couple of buses, were situated towards the Srebrenica direction and some buses also went towards Bratunac. That is how they left the enclave. The men were separated. If I could just show you in this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, referring to the same exhibit, 5/2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: So this is the area where the separation of the men took place [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for the record, it should indicate the witness showed the area around the White House.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the men's belongings. What happened to the men's belongings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: They were searched at such a high pace that all their belongings were taken away from them. The older men were put onto the bus -- the distinction was immediately made -- and the younger boys, around 15 up to 30 years, were taken apart. Some of them were interrogated, all their belongings were put onto one big heap, and afterwards, of course, they were also taken away, and it could be in both directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where the men were taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Most or all of them -- let me show you here in the picture -- were taken to the White House, across from the compound. That was a very distinctive location. Many military were around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were their belongings accumulating during this process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Their belongings were put near the entrance to this little house. Let me show you once more. Do you see the white bus here? That is the main entrance to the path leading to the White House, and that is where the belongings of all those people were put down. And in the end, it was such a big mound that around the White House everywhere there were those belongings, rucksacks, bags, shoes, passports, knives, razors, whatever they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicated a little white speck below the circle marked "White House." It appears to be an area in front of the White House.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier, you said that no one was in charge. Did you mean that no one was in charge from the Dutch or no one was in charge from the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: We were understaffed, and the higher-ranking officers and NCOs were under such stress and so busy with other things that we did not have any command. Everybody did as they saw best, and we did what we could. On the Serb side, it was certainly very well-organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What leads you to belief that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: It was certainly the case that it was a well-prepared stage. Everybody had been assigned a task, everybody knew his position. There were people who had to guard the compound, who had to guard the surroundings. There were units who had to clear out the houses, and there were other units who had to do the interrogations. Those were older men; most of them had a pistol. It was indeed well organised, and it was perhaps a separate unit assigned to this task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this unit that you think may have been a separate unit, what the people looked like, what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Around that White House, the interrogation house, there were mainly armed military in camouflage, and in the house, there were elder men with pistols. They had more experience. And there was certainly a good chain of command, who decided what was going to happen to those people and which bus they were to board. And, indeed, there was the police car, not the armed vehicle, but those Volkswagen Golfs. They were also present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this description you're giving us of various units all doing various tasks, including clearing out houses, guarding the compound, separating the men from the women and children, interrogating men, how would you describe the coordination between these various groups, as you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: From a military point of view, I would never condone what happened, but it was a good operation. It was well organised, well prepared, good command. Everybody knew their task. Certainly it was planned about how to go about this, and several units were involved for this approach. It was a large-scale approach in such a way that they did not know what resistance to expect, but they knew that they would be able to handle it as quickly as possible. There was good communication, internal communication, good liaison materiel, and it is well known, the Yugoslav army is well known for their good liaison materiel. It was very well organised. They had a sufficient chain of command. There was new materiel brought in, constantly new troops, new units, very well-oiled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see anyone in this room today that you saw out there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out where that person is and what they're wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Indicates]. He's sitting behind that gentleman. He has greying hair and he has a partition to the left. He is wearing a black jacket and a white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can the record indicate that he has identified General Krstic. And, Mr. President, as you've indicated, it's a good idea for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. McCloskey. I think that we have another one hour and five minutes to work, and I think we should split the remaining time in two parts. As far as I can see, there is an English interpreter who is working all the time, so we're going to have a break, a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, prior to the break, you'd identified General Krstic as a man that was present in Potocari during this time frame. When was the first time you saw General Krstic's face after seeing him in Potocari during this time frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: On the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That wasn't exactly my question, but I'll go back to that. So the first day being the day that the soldiers, the VRS soldiers, first arrived in Potocari, again, which day did you actually see General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: On the first day, the day of the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you saw him on the day that soldiers first came into the enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I also saw him once in front of the compound. At the time, he was together with several military, I think higher ranking ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him in front of the compound with other high-ranking military people, was that the first day or the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him on the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him on the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Around the compound, in the vicinity, and the White House, in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he doing when you saw him there on the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Mostly nothing. They didn't do much. They just looked whether everything was going according to plan. They didn't give any direct commands. It was all led by officers, by NCOs. It was already prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the first day you saw him with officers in the vicinity of the compound, what did you see that time, on that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The first day, they wanted to enter the compound, to see how many men there were at that moment in the compound, refugees who had been hiding in our compound. So they were kind of consulting at the gate whether they could enter or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they," again, who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The high-ranking military, security units who had to secure the officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And General Krstic was in that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The security was nervous because the compound was not yet secured. They were nervous, they thought there might be armed fighters inside. So they had not yet personally secured the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I need to go back and clarify the record. I didn't hear an answer to my question whether or not you saw General Krstic in that group of officers outside the compound.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes, he was also present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back to a question I asked a while back, when was the -- after seeing General Krstic in Potocari, how many days, weeks, or years later did you next -- was it until you next saw his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I've never, ever seen his face again, after those pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were shown some pictures, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you shown pictures of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: After I had been called to the Tribunal, those photographs were put in front of me, and I was asked whether I had ever seen this man before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was within the last two or three days, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm the person that showed you those photographs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's totally correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I showed you those photographs, were you able to recognise the person in the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same person that you see in court today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that the person you see in court today is the same person you saw in Potocari during the time period we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: No, I have no doubts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the separation process, did you witness any Serb troops using any violence against the men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: When I was outside the compound, standing outside the compound, the people were separated. It had to happen fast. There were older people amongst them and children, women with babies and with belongings. It was a hot day. They didn't have any water. If they didn't hurry, those people, sometimes they were kicked, they were beaten, they were pushed. Many people fell because of that, and some kind of traffic jams resulted. And they panicked. The buses were loaded so full that people were squashed inside the buses. They didn't get any water for the way, no food. The windows could not be opened. It was like a hot tin oven, it was so hot. Yes, indeed, there was kicking, beating, spitting, shouting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise any other Bosnian Serb officers present at Potocari on that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: General Mladic was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see Mladic doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: He was in the vicinity of the refugees, with lots of security guards. There was a camera crew there. They distributed candy. They acted kindly towards children and elderly people; they even patted their heads in front of the camera's eye, and they tried to act friendly, to be friendly. They said, "Don't worry. Nothing bad is going to happen, and you will be taken away to safety."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: After the camera crew stopped filming, the General turned around, he laughed. The soldiers took the candy back, took the cigarettes back. They spit at the children and at the women, and they were taken away directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides Krstic and Mladic, did you recognise any other Serb soldier or officer by name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. He said they were taken away directly. Who was taken away, and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The refugees who at that point in time were around the house, who had been given the candies, they were taken away immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Where? To where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: After the film crew had stopped, after the film had been taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just want to understand the word "away." To the buses? To the White House? Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Directly to the buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any other Bosnian Serb officer by name that was present in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Not by name, not directly by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness Exhibit 28-13.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct, I recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I saw him at OP Papa, at the time the convoys were not allowed to go through, and we negotiated with him, and I saw him on the day the enclave fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. To try to clear up -- you're talking about two different time periods now. One time period has to do with the convoys and convoys not being able to get through; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's correct. That was about halfway through my time in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at least some weeks prior to the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you next see this person in the exhibit, 28-13.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the compound and the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: He was also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was he doing in the vicinity of the refugees that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Not much. This man was standing there. He only talked to officers, not to subordinates. He was a quiet man. He certainly had a lot of authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to recognise any of the officers or Bosnian Serb soldiers you saw him talking to on that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The gentleman in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person you've identified in this courtroom previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... indicating General Krstic, for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw with General Krstic and this fellow, where they were, what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Those people had to laugh, and they found it all very jolly, what happened, in my opinion, at least. They were present in order to see that everything was going according to plan, and sometimes they gave commands, they gave orders, or they told people what to do, or it was reported to them how the situation was progressing. This group of persons mainly consisted of officers who watched the situation from the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic around these two people, General Krstic and this person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he involved in the discussions with them in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see a major who you had become familiar with prior to the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the name Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who's Major Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: He's a high-ranking officer with lots of authority. Well, at first sight, he's a friendly man, a fatherly type, also business-like type. Many subordinates became very nervous when he was around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you become familiar with Major Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand what the witness said. The interpreter is asking for the witness to start his statement again. Could you please ask the witness to repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for a minute. We have a little translation glitch, so let me ask you again. How did you know Major Nikolic? Where did you know him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: When I was at OP Papa, as an observer, we often went to the enclave's border as a kind of -- there was a kind of guardhouse, there were guards. Often we consulted about the convoys which were not allowed through, the convoys with food, and he was present often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Major Nikolic in Potocari on the first day, the day that Serb soldiers came in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes, he was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who he was with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Mainly with the high-ranking officers, and he had his own security guard. Mainly he drove in a blue Golf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to take you away from that first day and into the second day. Where did you spend the night of that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Where I spent the night is perhaps saying too much. We just kept on working. Mainly I was on the compound with the refugees, in the big hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever find any dead Muslims in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Mainly during the beginning of the evening, on the compound itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the first day or the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: From the first to the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The people on the compound were very frightened, they didn't know what to expect. Some people had hanged themselves. Actually, they had been -- they had injured themselves. There were dead babies lying, wrapped in clothes. There were bodies around, visible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next morning, what did you do, the morning of the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: We continued our day with our duties, in preparing the buses and trucks, to reconnoitre the vicinity. Those were our duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make a specific reconnoitre for some reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Several times I made a round of the compound, mainly in the hall where the injured people were, and indeed I was there several times and I saw a wounded soldier whom I had met before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I talked to that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: In English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: This soldier was about my age. We recognised each other, we knew each other from OP Sierra. He asked me what was going on outside and what was going to happen to him. He had injured himself; his arm, his leg, his head were injured. I asked, "What happened?" And he said, "I was in a fight with Serb military." I asked about his friend, because he had been with a friend before. His friend had been killed in a fight, and he had fled towards the compound. He asked me, "What's going to happen to me?" and I couldn't give him a direct answer to that. I mean, I could have done so, but it's very difficult to tell him that he, being a man, will be taken away, because separations are taking place. So I didn't tell him much. He said to me, "You don't have to tell me. I know what's going to happen. I'm going to be taken away and killed." So I just nodded my head and I saw the fear in his eyes. There wasn't much I could do. I stood powerless. And I haven't seen him since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the second day, did you go outside the compound on a patrol and find anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: On the second day, I indeed continued with my duties. Indeed, I walked around the compound, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And outside the compound, did you find anything significant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Outside the compound, many belongings were lying around, things belonging to people who had left their things people. I found passports, stuff, and bodies, dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you find the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Behind the White House, the interrogation house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any bodies up by a creek anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Behind the White House, about 700 metres from the compound, there is a kind of electricity house. I was very familiar with this route because I had patrolled it many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "behind the White House," are you referring to the bodies that you found in the creek, or were they other bodies actually right behind the White House?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Further away, behind the White House.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just found one group of bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes. I found nine -- I saw nine to ten corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to photograph them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to show the witness what has been marked OTP Exhibit 5/3A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take the green pen that you have in front of you and draw a circle around the area where you photographed these bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we put that on the ELMO so that we can all see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a creek in the vicinity of the area where you found the bodies, or a stream?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you mark -- do you recall where the stream was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark with a green pen where you recall the stream being?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you also circle the White House, as your recollection serves you, where it was on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Can you describe the situation, how it was that you came and found these bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: That day there had been rumours already, rumours about it being possible that there might be corpses in the vicinity. Shots had been heard in the whole area. And those were just rumours, actually. I had time to spare, and I just went into the area. I thought, "I won't go too far because I'm alone." Everybody else was busy, and anything could happen. "So if anything goes wrong, they will miss me straight away." And I met a colleague, he was higher in rank than I, and we started talking. And he asked me what I was doing there at that point in time, and I said, "Well, I heard a rumour of corpses being around here," and he said, "I also heard that." So after this exchange, we went on together and we took a path which went towards -- leading towards the location I circled, and there is where I found the bodies. So the rumour was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how close did you get to the bodies when you photographed them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I was on a hill, this brook or creek was about 20 metres away, and there were the bodies. My colleague was standing on guard because there were many Serb soldiers in the vicinity, those Rambo-types.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we show the witness Exhibit 59.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this -- number 59, is this one of the photographs that you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't come out very well on the ELMO, but there is a figure that's outlined with two white stripes. Were you the one that outlined that figure and those two white stripes over the photograph? Were you the one that outlined the figure with those two white stripes, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't come out on the ELMO at all, but could you just give your best effort to point at the photograph with your pointer and outline where you believe a figure is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: [Indicates]. This is his head, this black part is his hair, and this little white spot is his face. This man was wearing a blue vest over his white shirt. This is his blue vest. And this is his arm and a white shirt. This white part, this is the colour of his white shirt. Here is the creek, and this was the first man who was lying there, and the others were lying along that line here [indicates], downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, he indicated that the creek was below the figure of the person and that the line where the other bodies were lying was going from the figure left towards the right of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, sorry to interrupt you, but we are talking about the 12th of July. That is when the photograph was taken. I should like to know, when was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we clear up the actual date that this photograph was taken? If you don't know the date, was it the first day the soldiers came in or the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The second day. The first day, we were too busy with helping the refugees and there weren't many people walking around in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for insisting, but could you give us the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the actual date that this occurred? Excuse me. That you saw this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: The 12th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you able to take photographs of other bodies in the area, near this body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: I took several pictures of corpses which were lying there. These men were in a line, lying in a line, but as you can see yourselves, the foliage was very heavy and, to repeat again, I was on the ridge of the hill and there were many soldiers around. So I almost risked my own life in order to take these pictures, but, indeed, I took several pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're not a photographer, I take it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: As you can see from these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we show the witness Exhibit 60, and 61 shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, I think that we perhaps could adjourn after we see those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, prior to coming into court today, did you have a chance to study this photograph and mark certain outlines with white stripes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this one of the photographs you took, this number 60?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does seeing it help refresh your recollection about where the bodies were lying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's really impossible to tell from the photographs any bodies from this photograph, but have you attempted to outline your recollection of where the bodies were, from what you could see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you explain it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Here is the first victim [indicates], in our first picture. The second victim is lying here [indicates]; this man was wearing black clothes; here is where he was lying. Here is another victim [indicates]. This man is wearing white trousers. These are his legs and this is his face. To repeat, this is the direction of the stream, downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, for the record, the witness spoke of the first victim on the far left; the next he spoke of was in the middle; and the next was to the right of the middle person. And the stream is at the -- below the white markings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you also now look at number 61. Does the same hold true for 61? Is this a photograph that you previously looked at and had a chance to mark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is one of the photographs you took that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you can about this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F
utterances.text: Just to give you a picture, this is where the creek is running [indicates]. Here was a body, with his -- facing the creek, and here [indicates] another body. That's the first body in the first picture, the man wearing a blue vest, white sleeves, and black hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The record should indicate the first -- the body you discussed first on this photograph is to the left; the next body you discussed is to the right; and you pointed that the creek was down below both these bodies. Mr. President, this may be a good time to take the break or adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. McCloskey. We shall therefore adjourn, and tomorrow at half past nine, we shall be resuming. Until tomorrow, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
